articles.title: Vuelta a España: Tadej Pogacar punishes peloton with mighty solo win on stage four
articles.summary: Slovenian powers to victory by more than three minutes. Leader breaks rivals on brutal climb at halfway point. Tadej Pogacar crushed his Vuelta a España rivals to clinch a sensational solo stage four victory on Tuesday and open up a commanding general classification lead.
body: Tadej Pogacar arrived in red, lit the fuse on the climbs and turned stage four of the Vuelta a España ⁠into a private exhibition on Tuesday, powering away with almost 50 kilometres remaining to win alone in Andorra la Vella.

The Slovenian, bidding to ⁠complete his Grand ⁠Tour collection by ​claiming the Vuelta for the first time, attacked on the road to the second climb and quickly reduced a high-altitude battle into ⁠a one-man procession.

He began the final ascent with a lead of three minutes and 12 seconds and cruised over the last mountain pass before ⁠finishing in 2:40:35. Jarno Widar won the sprint for second, 2:39 off the pace, with Felix ​Gall third.

Seven years after his only previous ‌appearance in the Spanish ‌race, Pogacar underlined why he started as the overwhelming favourite following a summer in which ‌he claimed a fifth Tour de France title.

articles.title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
articles.summary: Cameroon international joins from Brighton. He says United are the ‘club of my dreams’ Manchester United have confirmed the signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton. The midfielder has signed a contract to 2031, with the option to extend by a year.
body: Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba has signed a five-year-deal with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.
Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer in which Casemiro has left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.
“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

articles.title: £1.5m-rated Abdulmalik asks to leave Boreham Wood
articles.summary: Boreham Wood forward Abdul Abdulmalik says he is "capable of reaching the top" after the National League side reject a £1.5m offer from Swedish club Djurgarden.
body: The 23-year-old has been the subject of serious interest from the Swedish top-flight side, who had an offer of £1m rejected earlier this month.
Boreham Wood do not want to sell Abdulmalik, with manager Luke Garrard saying "he is our player" after the forward was left out of the London club's 3-0 victory over Forest Green on Saturday.
"Everyone at Boreham Wood FC and the incredible fans have played a massive part [in my journey]. You will always have my respect," Adbulmalik said in a statement released by his agent.
"With this said, I'm ready for the next challenge. I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top."

articles.title: Ukrainian star leaves LSU women’s basketball team after signing of Russian recruit
articles.summary: Center Kate Koval departs after one season with Tigers. Anna Minaeva of Russia joined team earlier this month. Kim Mulkey hoped two could be ‘ambassadors’ for peace. Ukrainian center Kate Koval is leaving LSU less than two weeks after the Tigers brought in a player from Russia.
body: LSU coach Kim Mulkey said Monday night that Koval was leaving for “personal reasons”, adding that the program will “respect her privacy on her decision”.

“We had a long talk about it, and it was a hard decision for her,” Mulkey continued. “I know it is hard because she loves LSU. Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We all wish her the best.”

Koval, who was born in Kyiv and whose father serves in the Ukrainian military, began her college career at Notre Dame. She transferred before last season to LSU, where she averaged 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds and 16.6 minutes per game. Koval played high school basketball in New York, where she was one of the best young players in the country, and represented Ukraine at the Fiba 3x3 World Cup this summer.
Earlier this month, LSU signed Anna Minaeva, a 17-year-old who previously played professionally with MBA Moscow.

articles.title: Prime minister Andy Burnham ‘heartbroken’ after death of rugby league legend Billy Boston
articles.summary: Boston was one of the finest players in the sport’s history. Wigan plan series of tributes in Thursday’s Hull KR clash. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, said he is “heartbroken” by the passing of Sir Billy Boston as he lead tributes to the rugby league icon following his death.
body: Boston passed away on Tuesday at the age of 92. He was one of the sport’s all-time great players, scoring almost 500 tries during an illustrious career for Wigan Warriors and Great Britain, eventually becoming the first man in rugby league history to be knighted for his services to the game last year.

His death comes just four days after the funeral of his wife of over 70 years, Lady Joan Boston, who herself only passed away last month. Burnham, a lifelong rugby league supporter, who also served as president of the RFL, described Boston as a “giant of a man in every way”.

“Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died,” he wrote on Tuesday. “Billy was one of the greatest rugby league players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet.

“He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan. I will miss him greatly and am thinking today of Billy’s family, still grieving the recent loss of his beloved wife Joan. A giant of a man in every way. Thank you, Billy, and rest in peace.”

articles.summary: Sir Nick Faldo says LIV golfers seeking a return to the DP World Tour may have to "eat a bit of humble pie" before regaining eligibility for the European-based circuit.
body: LIV's 2026 season ended last Sunday in Indianapolis after this week's cancellation of the breakaway tour's Team Championship in Michigan.
Tyrrell Hatton, Tom McKibbin and Adrian Meronk are competing instead at the Husqvarna British Masters starting on Thursday.

Six-time major champion Faldo is promoting the Belfry tournament while LIV's boss Scott O'Neil continues his quest to replace Saudi Arabian funding. He wants $350m (£258m) investment to keep the league operating next year.
"I'm hearing there are more players wanting to leave LIV than want to stay," Faldo told BBC Sport.

articles.title: Warren thinks Fury-AJ fight will go ahead in America
articles.summary: Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.
body: Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.
Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".
However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.
Warren told Sky Sports News: "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

articles.title: Badgers up 26 spots in latest preseason rankings amid recent hype
articles.summary: The Wisconsin Badgers are looking to turn things around in 2026 after a couple of disappointing seasons, and there has been some growing optimism around the team this year.
body: Wisconsin still has to prove things on the field, and head coach Luke Fickell is still on the hot seat, but they’ll have the opportunity to get back on track with a better roster (on paper) and an easier schedule in 2026.

Well, that has led to the Badgers being one of the biggest risers in The Athletic’s preseason FBS rankings, jumping from No. 80, where they finished last season, to No. 54, falling just behind Vanderbilt (No. 51), UTSA (No. 52), and Tulane (No. 53).

“Coach Luke Fickell enters on the hot seat, but Old Dominion transfer quarterback Colton Joseph can provide a spark, and a defense that was legitimately good last year should still be solid,” The Athletic’s Chris Vannini wrote.

At No. 54, the Badgers are ahead of Nebraska (No. 58), Northwestern (No. 60), UCLA (No. 65), Michigan State (No. 72), Maryland (No. 73), Rutgers (No. 79), and Purdue (No. 97), ranking them No. 11 in the Big Ten.

articles.summary: All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.
body: Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.
Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.
He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

articles.title: 'Stupid mistakes' - Root 'hacked off' by latest off-field incident
articles.summary: A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.
body: England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.
